content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Status: deviation** (rule T4C — termination for convenience)

- **Vendor side is fine (better than preferred):** Section 7.1 prohibits Cellco from resigning as Servicer unless legally unable to perform, and Section 7.3 requires it to keep servicing until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement. No counterparty convenience exit — nothing to flag.
- **Customer side fails the fallback:** the only removal route is Section 7.2(c), which requires a continuing Servicer Termination Event (for cause) and is exercised by the Indenture Trustee. The Agreement runs until the last Receivable is paid in full (Section 8.3), far longer than 12 months, and the Optional Acquisition/Clean-Up Redemption and Optional Redemption rights sit with the Class A Certificateholder ("the Originators or their designee" — counterparty side) and require price agreement, so they are not our convenience exit.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** new Section 7.2A giving the Issuer a 30-day, no-fee convenience termination right with refund of prepaid amounts, effective only once a Successor Servicer accepts engagement under Section 7.4 so noteholder servicing continuity is preserved; 60 days offered as a fallback in the comment.
